GA resolutions are not a formal source of international law under Article 38(1) of the ICJ Statute, because they are generally non-binding recommendations. They can still matter as evidence of customary law (opinio juris) or as an aid to interpretation, as in *Nicaragua* and *Nuclear Weapons*, but only when backed by consistent state practice and a sense of legal obligation. The note's two options are both wrong, since resolutions neither always reflect custom nor equal treaties, though "reflect custom" is closer, and only in some cases.

CONFIDENCE: 88
